newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-SAMPRAS BREAKS HIS SWEDISH JINX.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS BREAKS HIS SWEDISH JINX.

text.p: The Swedish jinx which has dogged Pete Sampras all year was broken on Tuesday when the world number one thrashed Mikael Tillstrom in straight sets in Wimbledon's opening round.
Pistol Pete, experiencing the novelty of not opening the men's Centre Court action as defending champion for the first time in four years, beat Tillstrom 6-4 6-4 6-2 with the minimum of fuss.
Tillstrom came into Wimbledon with the reputation of one who knows how to cause an upset.
Last year he knocked out compatriot Stefan Edberg in the second round, spoiling the popular former champion's farewell party at his favourite tournament.

Sampras, who relinquished the title to Dutchman Richard Krajicek last year after winning it three times in a row, must have heaved a sigh when he saw the Wimbledon draw had given him a Swedish opponent first off.
Since winning the Australian Open title for the second time in January, the American has lost three times to Swedes.

Magnus Larsson beat him in the second round in Monte Carlo in April, Magnus Norman knocked him out of the third round at the French Open -- dashing his hopes of winning the only Grand Slam still to elude him -- and Jonas Bjorkman defeated him in the quarter-finals at London's Queen's Club earlier this month.
But Sampras was happy to see the back of Tillstrom and now prepares to meet German Hendrik Dreekmann.
The American, never one given to flamboyance or exuberance, is in quietly-confident mood.
"This is my place, this is where I am supposed to win," said Sampras. "It gives me confidence that I have won here before and I can do it again."

Sampras was feted for his previous achievements at the All England Club when he was invited to join a parade of former champions that also featured Rod Laver, John McEnroe and Boris Becker during the opening ceremony for the new Court One on Monday.
"I felt like I was part of a class of very good people," Sampras said on Tuesday. "It was an honour to be out there. It was something I will never forget."
